title.zh: 卷一百十八 列傳第五: 特薛禪 孛禿 阿剌兀思剔吉忽里
title.raw: 卷一百十八 列傳第五: 特薛禪 孛禿 阿剌兀思剔吉忽里 Volume 118 Biographies 5: Texuechan, Beitu, Alawusitijihuli

sentences.zh: 特薛禪，姓孛思忽兒，弘吉剌氏，世居朔漠。

translations.literal: Texuechan, surname Besihuer, of the Hongjila clan, for generations dwelt in the northern desert.
translations.idiomatic: Texuechan, of the Besihuer branch of the Hongjila clan, had lived for generations in the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 本名特，因從太祖起兵有功，賜名薛禪，故兼稱曰特薛禪。

translations.literal: His original name was Te; because he had merit following Taizu in raising troops, he was granted the name Xuechan, hence he was also called Texuechan.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Te, he earned the name Xuechan for meritorious service when Genghis Khan raised his army, and was thereafter known as Texuechan.

sentences.zh: 女曰孛兒台，太祖光獻翼聖皇后。

translations.literal: His daughter was Boertai, Taizus Radiant Offering Assisting Sagely Empress.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter Boertai became Genghis Khan's Radiant Offering Assisting Sagely Empress.

sentences.zh: 子曰按陳，從太祖征伐，凡三十二戰，平西夏，斷潼關道，取回紇尋斯干城，皆與有功。

translations.literal: His son was Anchannayan, who followed Taizu on campaigns—in all thirty-two battles, pacifying Western Xia, cutting the Tong Pass road, and taking the Uyghur city of Xingsigan—all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anchen followed Genghis Khan on thirty-two campaigns, helping pacify Western Xia, sever the Tong Pass route, and capture the Uyghur city of Xingsigan.

sentences.zh: 歲丁亥，賜號國舅按陳那顏。

translations.literal: In the dinghai year he was granted the title Imperial Uncle Anchannayan Noyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the dinghai year he received the title Imperial Uncle Anchannayan Noyan.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，賜銀印，封河西王，以統其國族。

translations.literal: In renchen he was granted a silver seal and enfeoffed King of Hexi to command his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: In renchen he received a silver seal and was enfeoffed King of Hexi to govern his people.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，賜錢二十萬緡，有旨：「弘吉剌氏生女世以為后，生男世尚公主，每歲四時孟月，聽讀所賜旨，世世不絕。」

translations.literal: In dingyou he was granted two hundred thousand strings of cash, with an edict: "Hongjila daughters shall generation after generation become empresses; Hongjila sons shall generation after generation marry imperial princesses; in the first month of each of the four seasons every year they shall hear the granted edict read—generation after generation without end."
translations.idiomatic: In dingyou he received two hundred thousand strings of cash along with an edict: "Hongjila daughters shall become empresses for generations; Hongjila sons shall marry imperial princesses for generations; in the first month of each season they shall hear this edict read—forever without end."

sentences.zh: 又賜所俘獲軍民五千二百，仍授萬戶以領之。

translations.literal: Again he was granted five thousand two hundred captured soldiers and civilians and appointed myriarch to command them.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted five thousand two hundred captured soldiers and civilians and appointed myriarch over them.

sentences.zh: 按陳薨，葬官人山。

translations.literal: Anchannayan died and was buried at Mount Guanren.
translations.idiomatic: Anchannayan died and was buried at Mount Guanren.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年二月，追封濟寧王，諡忠武；

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yuanzhen he was posthumously enfeoffed King of Jining with posthumous epithet Loyal Martial;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1295 he was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Jining with the epithet Loyal Martial;

sentences.zh: 妻哈真，追封濟寧王妃。

translations.literal: his wife Hazhen was posthumously enfeoffed Princess of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: his wife Hazhen was posthumously made Princess of Jining.

sentences.zh: 子斡陳，歲戊戌授萬戶，尚睿宗女也速不花公主。

translations.literal: His son Wochen, in the wuxu year appointed myriarch, married Ruizongs daughter Princess Yesubuhua.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wochen was appointed myriarch in wuxu and married Toluis daughter Princess Yesubuhua.

sentences.zh: 斡陳薨，葬不海韓。

translations.literal: Wochen died and was buried at Buhaihan.
translations.idiomatic: Wochen died and was buried at Buhaihan.

sentences.zh: 弟納陳，歲丁巳襲萬戶，奉旨伐宋，攻釣魚山。

translations.literal: His younger brother Nachan, in the dingsi year inheriting the myriarchate, received orders to attack Song and assault Diaoyu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Nachan inherited the myriarchate in dingsi, received orders to campaign against Song, and attacked Diaoyu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 又從世祖南涉淮甸，下大清口，獲船百餘艘。

translations.literal: Again he followed Shizu south across the Huai region, took Daqingkou, and captured more than a hundred vessels.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Kublai south across the Huai region, seized Daqingkou, and captured more than a hundred ships.

sentences.zh: 又率兵平山東濟、兖、單等州。

translations.literal: Again he led troops to pacify the Shandong prefectures Ji, Yan, Shan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He further led troops to pacify the Shandong prefectures of Ji, Yan, Shan, and others.

sentences.zh: 及阿里不哥叛，中統二年與諸王北伐，以其子哈海、脫歡、斡羅陳等十人自從，至于莽來，由失木魯與阿里不哥之黨八兒哈八兒思等戰，追北至孛羅克禿，復戰，自旦及夕，斬首萬級，僵尸被野。

translations.literal: When Ariq Böke rebelled, in the second year of Zhongtong he joined the northern campaign with the princes, taking ten of his sons including Hahai, Tuohuan, and Woluochen; reaching Manglai, from Shimur he fought Ariq Bökes partisan Baerhabaersi and others, pursued north to Boluoketu, fought again from dawn to evening, beheaded ten thousand ranks, and corpses covered the fields.
translations.idiomatic: When Ariq Böke rebelled, in 1261 he joined the princes on the northern campaign with ten sons including Hahai, Tuohuan, and Woluochen. At Manglai he fought Ariq Böke's partisan Baerhabaersi from Shimur, pursued north to Boluoketu, and fought again from dawn to dusk, taking ten thousand heads until corpses covered the plain.

sentences.zh: 薨，葬末懷禿。

translations.literal: He died and was buried at Mohuaitu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was buried at Mohuaitu.

sentences.zh: 斡羅陳襲萬戶，尚完澤公主。

translations.literal: Woluochen inherited the myriarchate and married Princess Wanzhe.
translations.idiomatic: Woluochen inherited the myriarchate and married Princess Wanzhe.

sentences.zh: 完澤公主薨，繼尚囊加真公主。

translations.literal: When Princess Wanzhe died he next married Princess Nangjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: After Princess Wanzhe died he married Princess Nangjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年薨，葬拓剌里。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan he died and was buried at Tuolali.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1277 and was buried at Tuolali.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

sentences.zh: 弟曰帖木兒，至元十八年襲萬戶。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Tiemuer; in the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan he inherited the myriarchate.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tiemuer inherited the myriarchate in 1281.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，乃顏叛，從帝親征，以功封濟寧郡王，賜白傘蓋以寵之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he followed the emperor on the personal campaign; for merit he was enfeoffed Prince of Jining Commandery and granted a white parasol canopy as favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when Nayan rebelled, he joined the emperor's personal campaign, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jining Commandery for his merit, and granted a white parasol canopy.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，諸王哈丹禿魯干叛，與諸王及統兵官玉速帖木兒等率兵討之，由龜剌河與哈丹等遇，轉戰至惱木連河，殲其眾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Prince Hadantuolugan rebelled; with princes and the commanding officer Yusutiemuer and others he led troops to suppress them; from Guila River he met Hadan and the rest, fought through to Naomulian River, and annihilated their forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, when Prince Hadantuolugan rebelled, he joined princes and the commander Yusutiemuer, met Hadan at the Guila River, fought through to the Naomulian River, and destroyed their army.

sentences.zh: 帝賜名按答兒禿那顏，以旌其功。

translations.literal: The emperor granted him the name Anchadartu Noyan to honor his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him the name Anchadartu Noyan to honor his achievement.

sentences.zh: 薨，葬末懷禿。

translations.literal: He died and was buried at Mohuaitu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was buried at Mohuaitu.

sentences.zh: 子二人：長曰琱阿不剌，次曰桑哥不剌，皆幼。

translations.literal: He had two sons: the elder Diaobubula and the younger Sangebubula—both young.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder Diaobubula and the younger Sangebubula, both still young.

sentences.zh: 至元二十七年，以其弟蠻子台襲萬戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Zhiyuan his younger brother Manzitai inherited the myriarchate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1290 his younger brother Manzitai inherited the myriarchate.

sentences.zh: 亦尚囊加真公主。

translations.literal: He also married Princess Nangjiazhen.
translations.idiomatic: He also married Princess Nangjiazhen.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，封皇姑魯國大長公主，以金印封蠻子台為濟寧王。

translations.literal: When Chengzong acceded, the imperial paternal aunt was enfeoffed Grand Princess of Lu; with a gold seal Manzitai was enfeoffed King of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: When Temür acceded, the imperial paternal aunt was made Grand Princess of Lu, and Manzitai was enfeoffed King of Jining with a gold seal.

sentences.zh: 奉旨率本部兵討叛王海都、篤哇，既與之遇，方約戰，行伍未定，單騎突入陣中，往復數四，敵兵大擾，一戰遂大捷。

translations.literal: By imperial order he led his tribes troops to suppress the rebel princes Qaidu and Duwa; having met them, just as battle was to be joined and ranks not yet set, he charged alone into the enemy array back and forth several times; the enemy troops were greatly thrown into disorder and one battle brought a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to lead his tribesmen against the rebel princes Qaidu and Duwa, he met the enemy just as battle was forming. Before the ranks were set he charged alone into their lines several times, threw them into disorder, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 時武宗在藩邸，統大軍以鎮朔方，有旨令蠻子台總領蒙古軍民官，轉武宗守莽來，以遏北方。

translations.literal: At that time Wuzong was at the princely residence commanding a great army to guard the northern frontier; an edict ordered Manzitai to take overall charge of Mongol military and civilian offices and transfer to Wuzongs garrison at Manglai to check the north.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wuzong was holding a princely command, leading a great army to guard the northern frontier; an edict ordered Manzitai to take overall charge of Mongol military and civilian offices and transfer to Wuzong's garrison at Manglai to check the north.

sentences.zh: 囊加真公主薨，繼尚裕宗女喃哥不剌公主。

translations.literal: When Princess Nangjiazhen died he next married Yuzongs daughter Princess Nangebubula.
translations.idiomatic: After Princess Nangjiazhen died he married Yuzongs daughter Princess Nangebubula.

sentences.zh: 蠻子台薨，年五十有二。

translations.literal: Manzitai died at age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Manzitai died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年三月，按答兒禿長子琱阿不剌襲萬戶，尚祥哥剌吉公主。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eleventh year of Dade, Anchadartus eldest son Diaobubula inherited the myriarchate and married Princess Xianggeleji.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1307, Anchadartus eldest son Diaobubula inherited the myriarchate and married Princess Xianggeleji.

sentences.zh: 六月，封大長公主，賜琱阿不剌金印，加封魯王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month she was enfeoffed Grand Princess; Diaobubula was granted a gold seal and further enfeoffed King of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month she was made Grand Princess; Diaobubula received a gold seal and was further enfeoffed as King of Lu.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，賜平江稻田一千五百頃。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida he was granted fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 he was granted fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 皇慶間，加封皇姊大長公主。

translations.literal: During Huangqing she was further enfeoffed Grand Princess, elder sister of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangqing she was further enfeoffed as the emperor's elder sister, Grand Princess.

sentences.zh: 天曆間，加號皇姑徽文懿貞壽大長公主。

translations.literal: During Tianli her title was further raised to Imperial Paternal Aunt, Grand Princess of Splendid Culture, Graceful Virtue, Chaste Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianli she received the further title Imperial Paternal Aunt, Grand Princess of Splendid Culture, Graceful Virtue, Chaste Longevity.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，琱阿不剌薨，葬末懷禿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida Diaobubula died and was buried at Mohuaitu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1310 Diaobubula died and was buried at Mohuaitu.

sentences.zh: 阿里嘉室利，琱阿不剌嫡子也。

translations.literal: Alijiashili was Diaobubulas legitimate son.
translations.idiomatic: Alijiashili was Diaobubulas legitimate son.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，甫八歲，襲萬戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhida, only eight years old, he inherited the myriarchate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1310, at only eight years of age, he inherited the myriarchate.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，襲封魯王，尚朵兒只班公主。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year he inherited enfeoffment as King of Lu and married Princess Duoerzhiban.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the following year he inherited the title King of Lu and married Princess Duoerzhiban.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，阿里嘉失利薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong Alijiashili died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1333 Alijiashili died.

sentences.zh: 至順間，封朵兒只班號肅雍賢寧公主。

translations.literal: During Zhishun Duoerzhiban was enfeoffed Princess Suoyong Xianning.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhishun Duoerzhiban was enfeoffed as Princess Suyong Xianning.

sentences.zh: 桑哥不剌者，魯王琱阿不剌之弟、阿里嘉室利之叔也。

translations.literal: Sangebubula was King of Lu Diaobubulas younger brother and Alijiashilis uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Sangebubula was the younger brother of King of Lu Diaobubula and uncle of Alijiashili.

sentences.zh: 自幼奉世皇旨，養于斡可珍公主所，是為不只兒駙馬，後襲統其本部民四百戶。

translations.literal: From youth by Shizu emperors order he was raised in Princess Wokezhens household and became the consort Bozhuer; later he inherited command of four hundred households of his tribes people.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood, by Kublai's order, he was raised in Princess Wokezhen's household and became the consort Bozhuer; later he inherited four hundred households of his tribe's people.

sentences.zh: 成宗時，奉旨尚普納公主；

translations.literal: In Chengzongs time by imperial order he married Princess Puna;
translations.idiomatic: Under Temür he was ordered to marry Princess Puna;

sentences.zh: 至順間，封鄆安大長公主，授桑哥不剌金印，封鄆安王，職千戶。

translations.literal: during Zhishun she was enfeoffed Grand Princess of Yun'an; Sangebubula was granted a gold seal and enfeoffed King of Yun'an with the office of chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: during Zhishun she was made Grand Princess of Yun'an; Sangebubula received a gold seal and was enfeoffed as King of Yun'an with a chiliarchate.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，授萬戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he was appointed myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: In 1333 he was appointed myriarch.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，加封鄆安公主號皇姑大長公主；

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year the Princess of Yun'an was further enfeoffed Imperial Paternal Aunt Grand Princess;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year the Princess of Yun'an was further titled Imperial Paternal Aunt, Grand Princess;

sentences.zh: 加封桑哥不剌魯王。

translations.literal: Sangebubula was further enfeoffed King of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: and Sangebubula was further enfeoffed as King of Lu.

sentences.zh: 以疾薨，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died of illness at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 此皆以駙馬襲封王爵者也。

translations.literal: These all inherited princely rank through service as imperial sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: These all inherited princely titles through imperial marriage.

sentences.zh: 唆兒火都者，亦按陳之子，以從征功，在太祖朝遙授左丞相，為千戶，仍賜以塗金銀章，及金銀字海青圓符五、驛馬券六。

translations.literal: Suo'erhuodu was also a son of Anchannayan; for merit on campaign, in Taizu's reign he was appointed from afar as Left Chancellor, made a chiliarch of a thousand households, and further granted a gilt silver seal, five gyrfalcon round tallies inscribed in gold and silver, and six relay-horse vouchers.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'erhuodu, another son of Anchannayan, distinguished himself on campaign. Under Genghis Khan he received a distant appointment as Left Chancellor, was made commander of a thousand households, and was further awarded a gilt silver seal, five inscribed gyrfalcon round tallies, and six imperial relay vouchers.

sentences.zh: 其子曰阿哈駙馬，當憲宗朝嘗率兵破徐州，以功受賞黃金一鋌、白金十鋌及銀鞍勒，仍命襲父官。

translations.literal: His son was the consort Aha; in Xianzong's reign he once led troops and captured Xuzhou; for merit he received one ingot of gold, ten ingots of white metal, and silver saddle and bridle fittings, and was ordered to succeed to his father's office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Aha, an imperial consort, led troops during Möngke's reign and seized Xuzhou. He was rewarded with one gold ingot, ten silver ingots, and silver saddle gear, and ordered to inherit his father's post.

sentences.zh: 至世祖時，有昭「弘吉剌萬戶所受驛券、圓符皆仍其舊，凡唆兒火都所受者，宜皆收之」，而唆兒火都之諸孫若孛羅沙、伯顏、蠻子、添壽不花、大都不花、掌吉等，及阿哈千戶之孫曰也速達兒與按陳之弟名冊者，在太祖世授官本藩蒙古軍站千戶。

translations.literal: By Shizu's time there was an edict: "The relay vouchers and round tallies held by the Hongjila chiliarch are to remain as before; all those held by Suo'erhuodu are to be collected." Suo'erhuodu's grandsons Boruosha, Bayan, Manzi, Tianshoubuhua, Dadubuhua, Zhangji, and others, as well as the grandson of the chiliarch Aha named Yesuda'er and Anchannayan's younger brother named Ce, had in Taizu's time received appointment in their own fief as chiliarchs of Mongol military relay posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kublai an edict declared: "The Hongjila chiliarch's relay vouchers and round tallies shall remain unchanged; Suo'erhuodu's shall be revoked." Suo'erhuodu's grandsons—including Boruosha, Bayan, Manzi, Tianshoubuhua, Dadubuhua, and Zhangji—as well as Aha's grandson Yesuda'er and Anchannayan's younger brother Ce had all been commissioned in Genghis Khan's time as chiliarchs of Mongol relay stations within their hereditary fief.

sentences.zh: 冊之子曰哈兒哈孫，以平金功，賜號拔都兒。

translations.literal: Ce's son was named Harhasun; for merit in pacifying the Jin he was granted the title Batuur.
translations.idiomatic: Ce's son Harhasun earned the heroic title Batuur for defeating the Jin.

sentences.zh: 哈兒哈孫之孫曰都羅兒，至元四年，授光祿大夫，以銀章封懿國公。

translations.literal: Harhasun's grandson was named Duoluo'er; in the fourth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and, with a silver seal, enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Harhasun's grandson Duoluo'er was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness in 1267 and enfeoffed as Duke of Yi with a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 有脫憐者，亦按陳之裔孫也，世祖授本藩千戶，仍賜驛券、圓符各四，令以兵守朔土之怯魯連。

translations.literal: There was one named Tuolian, also a descendant of Anchannayan; Shizu appointed him chiliarch of his own fief, further granted four relay vouchers and four round tallies each, and ordered him to garrison Qielulian in the northern frontier with troops.
translations.idiomatic: There was Tuolian, another descendant of Anchannayan. Kublai made him commander of a thousand households in his hereditary fief, granted four relay vouchers and four round tallies, and ordered him to garrison Qielulian on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，從族父按答兒禿征叛王乃顏有功，亦賜號拔都兒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, following his clansman Anchadartu in campaigning against the rebel prince Nayan, he had merit and was likewise granted the title Batuur.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he followed his kinsman Anchadartu against the rebel prince Nayan and distinguished himself, earning the heroic title Batuur.

sentences.zh: 脫憐卒，子迸不剌嗣。

translations.literal: Tuolian died; his son Bengbula succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuolian died, his son Bengbula succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 迸不剌卒，子買住罕嗣。

translations.literal: Bengbula died; his son Maizhuhan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Bengbula died, his son Maizhuhan inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 買住罕尚拜答沙公主。

translations.literal: Maizhuhan married Princess Baidasha.
translations.idiomatic: Maizhuhan married Princess Baidasha.

sentences.zh: 卒，弟孛羅帖木兒嗣，以金章封毓德王。

translations.literal: He died; his younger brother Boluotiemuer succeeded and, with a gold seal, was enfeoffed as King of Yude.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his younger brother Boluotiemuer succeeded and was enfeoffed as King of Yude with a gold seal.

sentences.zh: 孛羅帖木兒薨，買住罕孫阿失襲千戶。

translations.literal: Boluotiemuer died; Maizhuhans grandson Ash inherited the chiliarchate.
translations.idiomatic: When Boluotiemuer died, Maizhuhan's grandson Ash inherited the chiliarchate.

sentences.zh: 有名醜漢者，按陳次子必哥之裔孫，尚臺忽魯都公主。

translations.literal: There was one called Chouhan, a descendant of Anchannayan's second son Bike, who married Princess Taihupudu.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of Anchannayan's second son Bike, known as Chouhan, married Princess Taihupudu.

sentences.zh: 仁宗朝，封安遠王，以兵守莽來。

translations.literal: In Renzong's reign he was enfeoffed as King of Anyuan and stationed troops at Manglai.
translations.idiomatic: During Renzong's reign he was made King of Anyuan and garrisoned Manglai with his forces.

sentences.zh: 有答兒罕者，亦特薛禪之裔孫也，以從軍功，世祖亦賜以拔都兒之號，加賜黃金一鋌。

translations.literal: There was one Daerhan, also a descendant of Texuechan; for military merit Shizu likewise granted him the title Batuur and an additional gift of one gold ingot.
translations.idiomatic: Daerhan, another descendant of Texuechan, won military honors and received the Batuur title from Kublai along with an extra gold ingot.

sentences.zh: 其子曰不只兒，從征乃顏，禽其黨金家奴，帝賞以金帶。

translations.literal: His son was named Bozhuer; campaigning against Nayan he captured the rebel's partisan Jinjianu, and the emperor rewarded him with a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bozhuer joined the campaign against Nayan, seized the rebel partisan Jinjianu, and was awarded a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 其後有曰伯奢者，即其孫也。

translations.literal: Later there was one named Boshe, who was his grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Later there was Boshe, his grandson.

sentences.zh: 又按陳之孫納合，尚太宗唆兒哈罕公主。

translations.literal: Again, Anchannayan's grandson Nahe married Taizong's daughter Princess Suo'erhahan.
translations.idiomatic: Anchannayan's grandson Nahe married Ögedei's daughter Princess Suo'erhahan.

sentences.zh: 火忽之孫不只兒，尚斡可真公主。

translations.literal: Huohuo's grandson Bozhuer married Princess Wokezhen.
translations.idiomatic: Huohuo's grandson Bozhuer married Princess Wokezhen.

sentences.zh: 又特薛禪諸孫有名脫羅禾者，尚不魯罕公主，繼尚闊闊倫公主。

translations.literal: Again among Texuechan's grandsons there was one named Tuoluohe, who married Princess Buluhan and later Princess Kuokuolun.
translations.idiomatic: Among Texuechan's grandsons, Tuoluohe married Princess Buluhan and later Princess Kuokuolun.

sentences.zh: 此皆尚公主為駙馬者也。

translations.literal: These all married imperial princesses and became consorts.
translations.idiomatic: All of these men married imperial princesses and served as imperial consorts.

sentences.zh: 凡其女之為後者，自光獻翼聖皇后以降，憲宗貞節皇后諱忽都臺，及後妹也速兒，皆按陳從孫忙哥陳之女。

translations.literal: As for the women who became empresses, from the Radiant and Assisting Sagely Queen downward: Xianzong's Chaste and Constant Empress, tabooed Hudutai, and her younger sister Yesu'er, were all daughters of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Manggechen.
translations.idiomatic: Among the women who became empresses—beginning with the Radiant and Assisting Sagely Empress—Xianzong's Chaste and Constant Empress Hudutai and her sister Yesu'er were daughters of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Manggechen.

sentences.zh: 世祖昭睿順聖皇后諱察必，濟寧忠武王按陳之女；

translations.literal: Shizu's Sagacious and Farsighted Virtuous Sacred Empress, tabooed Chabi, was daughter of the loyal and martial King Anchannayan of Jining;
translations.idiomatic: Kublai's Sagacious and Farsighted Virtuous Sacred Empress Chabi was the daughter of Anchannayan, loyal and martial King of Jining;

sentences.zh: 其諱帖古倫者，按陳孫脫憐之女；

translations.literal: she tabooed Tiegulun, daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Tuolian;
translations.idiomatic: another bore the taboo name Tiegulun and was Anchannayan's grandson Tuolian's daughter;

sentences.zh: 諱喃必冊繼守正宮者，納陳孫仙童之女。

translations.literal: tabooed Nanbice, who succeeded in guarding the principal palace, was daughter of Nachen's grandson Xiantong.
translations.idiomatic: the empress tabooed Nanbice, who later held the principal palace, was Nachen's grandson Xiantong's daughter.

sentences.zh: 成宗貞慈靜懿皇后諱實憐答裏，斡羅陳之女也。

translations.literal: Chengzong's Chaste, Kind, Serene, and Gracious Empress, tabooed Shiliandali, was Woluochen's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong's Chaste, Kind, Serene, and Gracious Empress Shiliandali was Woluochen's daughter.

sentences.zh: 順宗昭獻元聖皇后諱答吉，大德十一年十一月，武宗冊上皇太后，至大三年十月，加上尊號曰儀天興聖慈仁昭懿壽元皇太后，仁宗延祐二年，加上尊號曰儀天興聖慈仁昭懿壽元全德泰寧福慶皇太后，延祐七年，又加徽文崇祐四字，尊號太皇太后，則按陳孫渾都帖木兒之女。

translations.literal: Shunzong's Sagely and Offering Primordial Sacred Empress, tabooed Daji—in the eleventh month of the eleventh year of Dade, Wuzong installed her as Grand Empress Dowager; in the tenth month of the third year of Zhida an honorific was added making her Grand Empress Dowager with the style 'Honoring Heaven, Rising Sage, Kind and Benevolent, Illustrious and Auspicious, Long-lived and Primordial'; in the second year of Yanyou, Renzong added further honorifics making her 'Grand Empress Dowager of Complete Virtue, Great Tranquility, and Fortunate Celebration'; in the seventh year of Yanyou four more characters of imperial commendation were added, raising her to Grand Empress Dowager—was daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Hundutiemuer.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzong's Sagely and Offering Primordial Sacred Empress Daji—enrolled as Empress Dowager by Wuzong in 1307, given added honorifics as Empress Dowager in 1310 and again under Renzong in 1315, and in 1320 raised to Grand Empress Dowager—was the daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Hundutiemuer.

sentences.zh: 武宗宣慈惠聖皇后諱真哥，脫憐子迸不剌之女；

translations.literal: Wuzong's Kind, Merciful, and Sagely Empress, tabooed Zhenge, was daughter of Tuolian's son Bingbula;
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong's Kind, Merciful, and Sagely Empress Zhenge was Tuolian's son Bengbula's daughter;

sentences.zh: 其諱速哥失裏者，按陳從孫哈兒只之女。

translations.literal: she tabooed Sugeshili was daughter of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Harzhi.
translations.idiomatic: another, tabooed Sugeshili, was daughter of Anchannayan's collateral descendant Harzhi.

sentences.zh: 泰定皇后諱八不罕，按陳孫斡留察兒之女；

translations.literal: Taiding's Empress, tabooed Babuhan, was daughter of Anchannayan's grandson Woluchu'er;
translations.idiomatic: Taiding's Empress Babuhan was Anchannayan's grandson Woluchu'er's daughter;

sentences.zh: 其諱必罕、諱速哥答裏者，皆脫憐孫買住罕之女。

translations.literal: those tabooed Bihan and Sugedali were both daughters of Tuolian's grandson Maizhuhan.
translations.idiomatic: those tabooed Bihan and Sugedali were both daughters of Tuolian's grandson Maizhuhan.

sentences.zh: 文宗皇后諱不答失裏，雕阿不剌魯王之女。

translations.literal: Wenzong's Empress, tabooed Budashili, was daughter of the King of Diaoa'abulu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong's Empress Budashili was daughter of Diaoa'bula, King of Lu.

sentences.zh: 此則弘吉剌氏之為後者也。

translations.literal: These, then, were Hongjila women who became empresses.
translations.idiomatic: These were the Hongjila women who ascended to the throne as empresses.

sentences.zh: 初，弘吉剌氏族居於苦烈兒、溫都兒斤、叠烈木兒、也裏古納河之地。

translations.literal: Initially the Hongjila clan dwelt in the lands of Külüer, Undurjin, Dielemur, and the Ergune River.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Hongjila people lived along the Külüer, Undurjin, Dielemur, and Ergune rivers.

sentences.zh: 歲甲戌，太祖在叠蔑可兒時，有旨分賜按陳及其弟火忽、冊等農土，

translations.literal: In the jiaxu year, when Taizu was at Diemieke'er, an order divided and granted nongtu to Anchannayan and his younger brothers Huohuo and Ce,
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year, when Genghis Khan was at Diemieke'er, an edict divided territorial grants among Anchannayan and his younger brothers Huohuo and Ce,

sentences.zh: 〈（農土猶言經界也。）〉

translations.literal: (Nongtu is equivalent to saying territorial boundaries.)
translations.idiomatic: (nongtu means territorial demarcation.)

sentences.zh: 若曰「是苦烈兒、溫都兒斤，以與按陳及哈撒兒為農土」。

translations.literal: as if saying "Let Külüer and Undurjin be nongtu for Anchannayan and Qasar."
translations.idiomatic: As if to say, "Let Külüer and Undurjin serve as territorial grants for Anchannayan and Qasar."

sentences.zh: 申諭按陳曰：「可木兒溫都兒、答兒腦兒、叠蔑可兒等地，汝則居之。」

translations.literal: He admonished Anchannayan: 'The places Komuer Undur, Da'erna'er, Diemieke'er, and the like—you shall dwell there.'
translations.idiomatic: He instructed Anchannayan: 'You shall settle at Komuer Undur, Da'erna'er, Diemieke'er, and the like.'

sentences.zh: 諭冊曰：「阿剌忽馬乞迤東，蒜吉納禿山、木兒速拓、哈海斡連直至阿只兒哈溫都、哈老哥魯等地，汝則居之。

translations.literal: He instructed Ce: 'East of Ala humaqu, from Suanjinatou Mountain, Mu'ersutuo, Haiwailian straight to Azhier Hawundu and Haolaogolu and the like—you shall dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: He told Ce: 'East of Ala humaqu, from Suanjinatou Mountain through Mu'ersutuo and Haiwailian to Azhier Hawundu and Haolaogolu—you shall dwell there.

sentences.zh: 當以胡盧忽兒河北為鄰，按赤臺為界。」

translations.literal: Take the north bank of the Huluhu'er River as neighbor, with Achitai as boundary.'
translations.idiomatic: Your neighbor shall be the north bank of the Huluhu'er River, with Achitai as the boundary.'

sentences.zh: 又諭火忽曰：「哈老溫迤東，塗河、潢河之間，火兒赤納慶州之地，與亦乞列思為鄰，汝則居之。」

translations.literal: Again he instructed Huohuo: 'East of Hawundu, between the Tu River and the Huang River, the land of Huo'erchin and Qingzhou, neighboring Yiqiliesi—you shall dwell there.'
translations.idiomatic: He further told Huohuo: 'East of Hawundu, between the Tu and Huang rivers—the lands of Huo'erchin and Qingzhou, bordering the Yiqiliesi—you shall settle there.'

sentences.zh: 又諭按陳之子唆魯火都曰：「以汝父子能輸忠於國，可木兒溫都兒迤東，絡馬河至於赤山，塗河迤南，與國民為鄰，汝則居之。」

translations.literal: Again he instructed Anchannayan's son Suoluhuodu: 'Because you father and son can render loyal service to the state, east of Komuer Undur, from the Luoma River to Chishan, south along the Tu River, neighboring the imperial subjects—you shall dwell there.'
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed Anchannayan's son Suoluhuodu: 'Because you and your father have served the state faithfully, you shall dwell east of Komuer Undur, from the Luoma River to Chishan, south along the Tu River, neighboring the imperial subjects.'

sentences.zh: 至至元七年，斡羅陳萬戶及其妃囊加真公主請於朝曰：「本藩所受農土，在上都東北三百里答兒海子，實本藩駐夏之地，可建城邑以居。」

translations.literal: By the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the myriarch Woluochen and his consort Princess Nangjiazhen petitioned the court: 'The nongtu our fief received, at Da'erhaizi three hundred li northeast of Shangdu, is in fact where our fief summers; a walled town may be built to dwell there.'
translations.idiomatic: In 1270 the myriarch Woluochen and his consort Princess Nangjiazhen petitioned the court: 'Our granted territory at Da'er Lake, three hundred li northeast of Shangdu, is our fief's summer encampment; we ask permission to build a walled town there.'

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 遂名其城為應昌府。

translations.literal: The city was then named Yingchang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The new city was named Yingchang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，改為應昌路。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year it was changed to Yingchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year it was changed to Yingchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，濟寧王蠻子臺亦尚囊加真公主，復與公主請於帝，以應昌路東七百里駐冬之地創建城邑，復從之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, Prince Jining Manzitai also married Princess Nangjiazhen; again together with the princess they petitioned the emperor to establish a walled town at the wintering site seven hundred li east of Yingchang Circuit, and again he assented.
translations.idiomatic: In 1295 Prince Jining Manzitai also married Princess Nangjiazhen; together they petitioned the emperor to build a town at their winter camp seven hundred li east of Yingchang Circuit, and again he agreed.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，名其城為全寧路。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade the city was named Quanning Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1297 that city was named Quanning Circuit.

sentences.zh: 弘吉剌之分邑，得任其陪臣為達魯花赤者，有濟寧路及濟、兖、單三州，鉅野、鄆城、金鄉、虞城、碭山、豐縣、肥城、任城、魚臺、沛縣、單父、嘉祥、磁陽、寧陽、曲阜、泗水一十六縣。

translations.literal: Among Hongjila sub-fiefs where attendant ministers might be appointed darughachi, there were Jining Circuit together with the three prefectures Ji, Yan, and Shan, and sixteen counties: Juye, Yuncheng, Jinxiang, Yucheng, Dangshan, Fengxian, Feicheng, Rencheng, Yutai, Peixian, Shanfu, Jiaxiang, Ciyang, Ningyang, Qufu, and Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Hongjila sub-fiefs whose attendant ministers could serve as darughachi were Jining Circuit and the three prefectures of Ji, Yan, and Shan, together with sixteen counties: Juye, Yuncheng, Jinxiang, Yucheng, Dangshan, Feng, Feicheng, Rencheng, Yutai, Pei, Shanfu, Jiaxiang, Ciyang, Ningyang, Qufu, and Sishui.

sentences.zh: 此丙申歲之所賜也。

translations.literal: This was granted in the bingshen year.
translations.idiomatic: This grant dated to the bingshen year.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，陞古濟州為濟寧府，十八年始陞為路，而濟、兖、單三州隸焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan ancient Jizhou was promoted to Jining Prefecture; only in the eighteenth year was it first promoted to a circuit, and the three prefectures Ji, Yan, and Shan were placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1269 ancient Jizhou was elevated to Jining Prefecture; in 1281 it became a circuit, with Ji, Yan, and Shan prefectures subordinate to it.

sentences.zh: 又汀州路長汀、寧化、清流、武平、上杭、連城六縣，此至元十三年之所賜也。

translations.literal: Again Tingzhou Circuit had the six counties Changting, Ninghua, Qingliu, Wuping, Shanghang, and Liancheng; this was granted in the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhou Circuit with its six counties—Changting, Ninghua, Qingliu, Wuping, Shanghang, and Liancheng—was granted in 1276.

sentences.zh: 又有永平路灤州、盧龍、遷安、撫寧、昌黎、石城、樂亭六縣，此至大元年之所賜也。

translations.literal: Again Yongping Circuit had Luanzhou and the six counties Lulong, Qianan, Funing, Changli, Shicheng, and Leting; this was granted in the first year of Zhida.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping Circuit, Luanzhou, and the six counties of Lulong, Qianan, Funing, Changli, Shicheng, and Leting were granted in 1308.

sentences.zh: 若平江稻田一千五百頃，則至大二年所賜也。

translations.literal: As for fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang, that was granted in the second year of Zhida.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen hundred qing of rice paddies in Pingjiang were granted in 1309.

sentences.zh: 其應昌、全寧等路則自達魯花赤總管以下諸官屬，皆得專任其陪臣，而王人不與焉。

translations.literal: As for Yingchang, Quanning, and other circuits, from the darughachi and supervisor downward all offices could be filled exclusively by their attendant ministers, while princes of the blood did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingchang, Quanning, and similar circuits, every office from darughachi and supervisor downward could be held solely by attendant ministers, without involvement of imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 此外，復有王傅府，自王傅六人而下，其群屬有錢糧、人匠、鷹房、軍民、軍站、營田、稻田、煙粉千戶、總管、提舉等官，以署計者四十餘，以員計者七百餘，此可得而稽考者也。

translations.literal: Beyond this there was again the Prince's Tutorate; from six Prince Tutors downward their subordinates had offices for revenue grain, artisans, hawk chambers, military and civilian registry, relay posts, garrison fields, rice paddies, tobacco and powder chiliarchs, supervisors, intendants, and the like—more than forty agencies by establishment, more than seven hundred officers by headcount; these can be verified by examination.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this stood the Prince's Tutorate. Below its six tutors were subordinate offices for revenue, artisans, hawking, military and civilian affairs, relay stations, garrison farms, rice paddies, and tobacco—more than forty agencies in all and more than seven hundred officers, all of which can be verified in the records.

sentences.zh: 其五戶絲、金鈔之數，則丙申歲所賜濟寧路之三萬戶，至元十八年所賜汀州路之四萬戶，絲以斤計者，歲二千二百有奇；

translations.literal: As for the quantities of five-households silk and gold notes, the thirty thousand households granted to Jining Circuit in the bingshen year, and the forty thousand households granted to Tingzhou Circuit in the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan—silk reckoned in jin came to somewhat more than twenty-two hundred yearly;
translations.idiomatic: Their allotments of five-household silk and paper money included thirty thousand households granted to Jining Circuit in the bingshen year and forty thousand granted to Tingzhou Circuit in 1281—yielding somewhat more than twenty-two hundred jin of silk annually;

sentences.zh: 鈔以錠計者，歲一千六百有奇。

translations.literal: notes reckoned in ingots came to somewhat more than sixteen hundred yearly.
translations.idiomatic: and somewhat more than sixteen hundred ingots of paper money each year.

sentences.zh: 此則所謂歲賜者也。

translations.literal: This was what was called the annual gift.
translations.idiomatic: This was their so-called annual stipend.

sentences.zh: ○孛禿

translations.literal: ○ Beitu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Beitu

sentences.zh: 孛禿，亦乞列思氏，善騎射。

translations.literal: Beitu, of the Yiqiliesi clan, excelled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Beitu, of the Yiqiliesi clan, was a skilled mounted archer.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗潛遣術兒徹丹出使，至也兒古納河。

translations.literal: Taizu once secretly sent Shi'erchedan as envoy to the Ergune River.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan once secretly dispatched Shi'erchedan as an envoy to the Ergune River.

sentences.zh: 孛禿知其為帝所遣，值日暮，因留止宿，殺羊以享之。

translations.literal: Beitu knew he had been sent by the emperor; as night fell he detained him for lodging and killed a sheep to entertain him.
translations.idiomatic: Beitu recognized him as the emperor's envoy. At nightfall he detained him as a guest, slaughtered a sheep, and entertained him.

sentences.zh: 術兒徹丹馬疲乏，復假以良馬。

translations.literal: Shi'erchedan's horse was weary; he lent him a good horse in turn.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi'erchedan's horse was exhausted, Beitu lent him a fine mount.

sentences.zh: 及還，孛禿待之有加。

translations.literal: When he returned, Beitu treated him with added generosity.
translations.idiomatic: On his return journey Beitu treated him with even greater hospitality.

sentences.zh: 術兒徹丹具以白帝，帝大喜，許妻以皇妹帖木倫。

translations.literal: Shi'erchedan reported everything to the emperor; the emperor was greatly pleased and promised Beitu marriage to the imperial younger sister Tiemulun.
translations.idiomatic: Shi'erchedan reported all of this to the emperor, who was delighted and promised Beitu marriage to his younger sister Tiemulun.

sentences.zh: 孛禿宗族乃遣也不堅歹等詣太祖，因致言曰：「臣聞威德所加，若雲開見日、春風解凍，喜不自勝。」

translations.literal: Beitu's clansmen then sent Yebujianai and others to Taizu, conveying words: 'Your servant has heard that where majesty and virtue are applied, it is like clouds parting to reveal the sun and spring wind thawing ice; joy beyond bearing.'
translations.idiomatic: Beitu's clan then sent Yebujianai and others to Genghis Khan with this message: 'We hear that wherever your majesty and virtue reach, it is like clouds parting to reveal the sun or spring thawing the ice—we are overcome with joy.'

sentences.zh: 帝問：「孛禿孳畜幾何？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: 'How much livestock does Beitu possess?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, 'How much livestock does Beitu own?'

sentences.zh: 也不堅歹對曰：「有馬三十匹，請以馬之半為聘禮。」

translations.literal: Yebujianai replied: 'There are thirty horses; I request half the horses as betrothal gift.'
translations.idiomatic: Yebujianai answered, 'Thirty horses—we offer half as betrothal gifts.'

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「婚姻而論財，殆若商賈矣。

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: 'To discuss property in marriage is almost like merchants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry. 'To haggle over property in marriage is the way of merchants.

sentences.zh: 昔人有言，同心實難，朕方欲取天下，汝亦乞列思之民，從孛禿效忠於我可也，何以財為！」

translations.literal: In old times someone said that unity of heart is truly difficult; I am just now about to take the realm under Heaven—you too are people of Yiqiliesi; follow Beitu in rendering loyal service to me; why need property!'
translations.idiomatic: Someone once said that true unity of heart is rare. I am about to take the realm under Heaven—you are Yiqiliesi people; follow Beitu and serve me faithfully. What need is there for property!'

sentences.zh: 竟以皇妹妻之。

translations.literal: In the end he gave him the imperial younger sister in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he gave him his younger sister in marriage.

sentences.zh: 既而劄赤剌歹劄木哈、脫也等以兵三萬入寇。

translations.literal: Thereafter Zhachiladi Zhamuha, Tuoye, and others invaded with thirty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhachiladi Zhamuha, Tuoye, and others invaded with thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 孛禿聞之，遣波欒歹、磨裏禿禿來告，乃與哈剌裏、劄剌兀、塔兒哈泥等討脫也等，掠其輜重，降其民。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Beitu sent Bolundai and Molitutu to report; then with Harali, Zhalawu, Ta'erhani, and others he attacked Tuoye and the rest, seizing their baggage train and reducing their people.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Beitu sent Bolundai and Molitutu to report; then with Harali, Zhalawu, Ta'erhani, and others he attacked Tuoye's forces, seized their baggage train, and subdued their people.

sentences.zh: 乃蠻叛，帝召孛禿以兵至，大戰敗之。

translations.literal: When the Naiman rebelled, the emperor summoned Beitu with troops; in a great battle they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Naiman rebelled, the emperor summoned Beitu with troops and defeated them in a great battle.

sentences.zh: 皇妹薨，復妻以皇女火臣別吉，而命哈兒八臺之子也可忽林圖帶弓矢為之侍。

translations.literal: The imperial younger sister died; he again married him to the imperial daughter Huochenbieji, and ordered Haribatai's son Yehuohulin to carry bow and arrows as his attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial younger sister died, the emperor gave him his daughter Huochenbieji in marriage and appointed Haribatai's son Yehuohulin to attend him bearing bow and arrows.

sentences.zh: 哈兒八臺曰：「吾兒豈能為人臣仆，寧死不為也！」

translations.literal: Haribatai said: 'Can my son be another man's servant? Better death than that!'
translations.idiomatic: Haribatai declared, 'My son will never be another man's servant—I would rather see him dead!'

sentences.zh: 帝令孛禿與之敵，哈兒八臺令月列等拒戰於碗圖河。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Beitu to oppose him; Haribatai ordered Yuelie and others to resist at the Wantu River.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Beitu to fight him. Haribatai sent Yuelie and others to resist at the Wantu River.

sentences.zh: 孛禿直前擒月列，剌殺也可忽林圖，哈兒八臺走渡拙赤河，又擒之，盡殺其眾。

translations.literal: Beitu charged forward and captured Yuelie, stabbed and killed Yehuohulin; Haribatai fled across the Zhuochi River and was again captured; he killed all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Beitu charged forward, seized Yuelie, and stabbed Yehuohulin to death. Haribatai fled across the Zhuochi River but was captured again, and all his followers were slain.

sentences.zh: 從太師國王木華黎略地遼東、西，以功封冠懿二州。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Preceptor and King Muqali in overrunning the eastern and western Liao regions, for merit he was enfeoffed with the two prefectures Guan and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Grand Preceptor and King Muqali in campaigns across eastern and western Liao and was enfeoffed with Guan and Yi prefectures for his merit.

sentences.zh: 從征西夏，病薨。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Western Xia, he died of illness en route.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness while campaigning against Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠宣力佐命功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、駙馬都尉、上柱國，進封昌王，謚忠武。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted the merit titles Loyal and Upright in Supporting the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Holder of the Office of Equal Ranks with the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State; advanced enfeoffment to King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles Loyal and Upright in Supporting the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State, advanced to King of Chang with the posthumous epithet Loyal Martial.

sentences.zh: 子鎖兒哈襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Suo'erha inherited the rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Suo'erha inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 鎖兒哈，事太宗。

translations.literal: Suo'erha served Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'erha served Ögedei.

sentences.zh: 與木華黎取嘉州，降其民，遣伯禿兒哈拙赤碣來獻捷，帝曰：「若父宣力國家，朕昔見之。

translations.literal: With Muqali he took Jiazhou and reduced its people; he sent Botu'erhazhuochijie to present the victory report. The emperor said: 'Your father exerted strength for the state; I once saw him.
translations.idiomatic: With Muqali he captured Jiazhou and subdued its people, then sent Botu'erhazhuochijie to report the victory. The emperor said, 'Your father served the state with distinction—I knew him well.

sentences.zh: 今鎖兒哈克光前烈。」

translations.literal: Now Suo'erha can emulate his ancestors' brilliance.'
translations.idiomatic: Now Suo'erha honors his forebears' achievements.'

sentences.zh: 賜以金錦、金帶、七寶鞍，召至中都，以疾薨。

translations.literal: He was granted gold brocade, gold belt, and seven-jeweled saddle, summoned to the Central Capital, and died of illness there.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with gold brocade, a gold belt, and a seven-jeweled saddle, summoned to the Central Capital, and died of illness there.

sentences.zh: 鎖兒哈娶皇子斡赤女安禿公主，生女，是為憲宗皇后。

translations.literal: Suo'erha married Prince Woqi's daughter Princess Antu; a daughter was born who became Xianzong's empress.
translations.idiomatic: Suo'erha married Prince Woqi's daughter Princess Antu; their daughter became Möngke's empress.

sentences.zh: 子劄忽兒臣，從定宗出討萬奴有功，太宗命親王安赤臺以女也孫真公主妻之。

translations.literal: His son Zhahuerichen, following Dingzong in punitive expedition against Wantu with merit, Taizong ordered Imperial Prince Anchitai to give his daughter Princess Yesunzhen in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhahuerichen accompanied Güyük on the punitive expedition against Wantu and distinguished himself. Ögedei had Imperial Prince Anchitai give him his daughter Princess Yesunzhen in marriage.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈推誠靖宣佐運贊治功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、駙馬都尉、上柱國，襲封昌王，謚忠靖。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Sincere in Supporting the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Holder of the Office Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State; inherited enfeoffment as King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously granted the titles Sincere in Supporting the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State, and inherited the title King of Chang with the posthumous epithet Loyal and Tranquil.

sentences.zh: 劄忽兒臣有子二人：長月列臺，娶皇子賽因主卜女哈答罕公主，生脫別臺，與乃顏戰，有功。

translations.literal: Zhahuerichen had two sons: the elder Yuelietai married Prince Saiyinzhubu's daughter Princess Hadahan; begot Tuobietai, who fought Nayan with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhahuerichen had two sons. The elder, Yuelietai, married Prince Saiyinzhubu's daughter Princess Hadahan and fathered Tuobietai, who distinguished himself fighting Nayan.

sentences.zh: 次忽憐。

translations.literal: The younger was Hulian.
translations.idiomatic: The younger was Hulian.

sentences.zh: 忽憐，尚憲宗女伯牙魯罕公主。

translations.literal: Hulian married Xianzong's daughter Princess Boyaluohan.
translations.idiomatic: Hulian married Möngke's daughter Princess Boyaluohan.

sentences.zh: 後脫黑帖木兒叛，世祖命忽憐與失列及等討之，大戰終日，脫黑帖木兒敗走，帝嘉之，復令尚憲宗孫女不蘭奚公主。

translations.literal: Later when Tuheitie'muer rebelled, Shizu ordered Hulian with Shilieji and others to suppress him; they fought a full day; Tuheitie'muer fled in defeat; the emperor praised him and again had him marry Xianzong's granddaughter Princess Bulanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tuheitie'muer rebelled, Kublai ordered Hulian and Shilieji to suppress him. After a full day of fighting Tuheitie'muer fled. The emperor praised Hulian and gave him Möngke's granddaughter Princess Bulanxi in marriage.

sentences.zh: 宋平，封以廣州。

translations.literal: When the Song were pacified, he was enfeoffed with Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song were pacified, he was enfeoffed with Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乃顏、聲剌哈兒叛，世祖新征，薛徹堅等與哈答罕屢戰，帝召忽憐至。

translations.literal: When Nayan and Shenglaha'er rebelled, Shizu was newly on campaign; Xuechejian and others fought repeatedly with Hadahan; the emperor summoned Hulian.
translations.idiomatic: When Nayan and Shenglaha'er rebelled, Kublai was on campaign. Xuechejian and others fought repeatedly with Hadahan, and the emperor summoned Hulian.

sentences.zh: 值薛徹堅等戰於程火失溫之地，哈答罕眾甚盛，忽憐以兵二百迎敵，敗之。

translations.literal: When Xuechejian and others fought at Chenghuoshiwen, Hadahan's forces were very strong; Hulian with two hundred men met the enemy and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuechejian and others fought at Chenghuoshiwen, Hadahan's forces were overwhelming; Hulian met them with two hundred men and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 哈答罕等走度猱河，還其巢穴。

translations.literal: Hadahan and others fled across the Nuoy River and returned to their lair.
translations.idiomatic: Hadahan and his men fled across the Nuoy River and retreated to their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 逾年夏，帝命忽憐復征之。

translations.literal: The next summer the emperor ordered Hulian again to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer the emperor ordered Hulian to campaign against them again.

sentences.zh: 至曲列兒、塔兀兒二河之間，大戰，其眾皆度塔兀河遁去。

translations.literal: Between the Qulie'er and Ta'u'er rivers they fought a great battle; all his forces crossed the Ta'u River and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Qulie'er and Ta'u'er rivers they fought a great battle, and the enemy forces all fled across the Ta'u River.

sentences.zh: 余百人逃匿山谷，忽憐即率兵二百徒步追之。

translations.literal: More than a hundred men hid in mountain valleys; Hulian immediately led two hundred men on foot in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred fugitives hid in the valleys; Hulian immediately led two hundred men on foot in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 薛徹堅止之曰：「彼亡命者，安得徒行。」

translations.literal: Xuechejian stopped him, saying: 'Those fugitives—how could they travel on foot.'
translations.idiomatic: Xuechejian tried to stop him, saying, 'Those fugitives cannot possibly travel on foot.'

sentences.zh: 忽憐不聽，往殺其眾。

translations.literal: Hulian would not listen and went to kill their force.
translations.idiomatic: Hulian would not listen and went to slaughter them.

sentences.zh: 薛徹堅以聞，賜金一鋌、銀五鋌。

translations.literal: Xuechejian reported it; he was granted one ingot of gold and five of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Xuechejian reported the victory, and Hulian was rewarded with one gold ingot and five silver ingots.

sentences.zh: 又逾年，復往征之，與哈答罕遇於兀剌河。

translations.literal: Another year passed and he again went on campaign; he met Hadahan at the Wula River.
translations.idiomatic: Another year later he campaigned again and encountered Hadahan at the Wula River.

sentences.zh: 忽憐夜率千人潛入其軍，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Hulian at night led a thousand men to infiltrate his army and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Hulian led a thousand men in a night raid on the enemy camp and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 帝賜鈔五萬貫、金一鋌、銀十鋌。

translations.literal: The emperor granted fifty thousand strings of paper money, one ingot of gold, and ten of silver.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded him with fifty thousand strings of paper money, one gold ingot, and ten silver ingots.

sentences.zh: 忽憐薨，贈效忠保德輔運佐理功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、駙馬都尉、上柱國，追封昌王，謚忠宣。

translations.literal: When Hulian died he was posthumously granted the merit titles Effecting Loyalty in Preserving Virtue in Supporting Transport and Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State; posthumously enfeoffed King of Chang with posthumous epithet Loyal and Proclaiming.
translations.idiomatic: At Hulian's death he was posthumously granted the titles Effecting Loyalty in Preserving Virtue in Supporting Transport and Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Consort Commandant, and Chief Pillar of State, and posthumously enfeoffed as King of Chang with the epithet Loyal and Proclaiming.

sentences.zh: 子阿失，事成宗。

translations.literal: His son Ash served Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ash served Temür.

sentences.zh: 篤哇叛于海都，帝遣晉王甘麻剌并武宗帥師討之。

translations.literal: When Duwa rebelled alongside Qaidu, the emperor dispatched Prince of Jin Gamala together with Wuzong to command troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Duwa rebelled with Qaidu, the emperor sent Prince of Jin Gamala and Wuzong at the head of an army to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，戰哈剌答山，阿失射篤哇中其膝，擒殺甚多，篤哇號哭而遁，武宗賜之衣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade they fought at Mount Halada; Ash shot Duwa in the knee, captured and killed many; Duwa wailed and fled; Wuzong granted him clothing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1301 at Mount Halada, Ash shot Duwa in the knee, killed or captured many of his men, and drove Duwa off in tears; Wuzong rewarded him with garments.

sentences.zh: 成宗加賜珠衣，封為昌王，置王府官屬。

translations.literal: Chengzong further granted pearl garments, enfeoffed him as King of Chang, and established princely household offices.
translations.idiomatic: Temür added pearl robes, enfeoffed him as King of Chang, and established a princely household staff.

sentences.zh: 仁宗朝，復賜以寧昌縣稅入。

translations.literal: In Renzong's reign he was again granted the tax revenue of Ningchang County.
translations.idiomatic: Under Renzong he was again granted the tax revenue of Ningchang County.

sentences.zh: 阿失尚成宗女亦里哈牙公主，復尚憲宗曾孫女買的公主。

translations.literal: Ash married Chengzongs daughter Princess Yilihaya and later Möngkes great-granddaughter Princess Maide.
translations.idiomatic: Ash married Temür's daughter Princess Yilihaya and later Möngke's great-granddaughter Princess Maide.

sentences.zh: 阿失薨，子八剌失里襲封昌王。

translations.literal: Ash died; his son Balashili inherited enfeoffment as King of Chang.
translations.idiomatic: When Ash died, his son Balashili inherited the title King of Chang.

sentences.zh: 忽憐從弟不花，尚世祖女兀魯真公主；

translations.literal: Hulians younger cousin Buhua married Shizus daughter Princess Wuluzhen;
translations.idiomatic: Hulian's cousin Buhua married Kublai's daughter Princess Wuluzhen;

sentences.zh: 其弟鎖郎哈，娶皇子忙哥剌女奴兀倫公主，生女，是為武宗仁獻章聖皇后，實生明宗。

translations.literal: his younger brother Suolangha married Prince Mangge'as daughter Princess Nuwulun; the daughter born was Wuzongs Benevolent Offering Sagely Empress, who in fact bore Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Suolangha married Prince Mangge'a's daughter Princess Nuwulun; their daughter became Wuzong's Benevolent Offering Sagely Empress and bore Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 阿剌兀思剔吉忽裏，汪古部人，系出沙陀雁門之後。

translations.literal: Alawusitijihuli, a man of the Onggut tribe, traced his lineage to the Shatuo of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Alawusitijihuli, of the Onggut tribe, traced his descent to the Shatuo of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 遠祖卜國，世為部長。

translations.literal: A remote ancestor named Bokuo for generations was chief of the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: A remote ancestor named Bokuo had served for generations as chief of the tribe.

sentences.zh: 金源氏塹山為界，以限南北，阿剌兀思剔吉忽裏以一軍守其沖要。

translations.literal: The Jin used mountains as ramparts to divide north from south; Alawusitijihuli with one army guarded the strategic point.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin had built mountain ramparts to divide north from south, and Alawusitijihuli garrisoned the strategic pass with an army.

sentences.zh: 時西北有國曰乃蠻，其主太陽可汗遣使來約，欲相親附，以同據朔方。

translations.literal: At that time in the northwest there was a state called Naiman; its ruler the Sun Khan sent envoys to propose alliance, wishing mutual attachment to hold the northern frontier together.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Naiman state lay to the northwest; its ruler, the Sun Khan, sent envoys proposing an alliance so they might together hold the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 部眾有欲從之者，阿剌兀思剔吉忽裏弗從，乃執其使，奉酒六尊，具以其謀來告太祖。

translations.literal: Among the tribesmen some wished to follow; Alawusitijihuli would not follow; he then seized their envoys, presented six vessels of wine, and fully reported their plot to Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his tribesmen wished to accept, but Alawusitijihuli refused. He seized the envoys, presented six vessels of wine, and reported their entire plot to Genghis Khan.

sentences.zh: 時朔方未有酒，太祖飲三爵而止，曰：「是物少則發性，多則亂性。」

translations.literal: At that time the northern frontier had no wine; Taizu drank three goblets and stopped, saying: 'This substance in small amount stirs the nature, in large amount disorders the nature.'
translations.idiomatic: Wine was then unknown in the north. Genghis Khan drank three cups and stopped, saying, "A little of this rouses the spirit; too much disorders it."

sentences.zh: 使還，酬以馬五百、羊一千，遂約同攻太陽可汗。

translations.literal: He sent the envoys back, rewarded them with five hundred horses and a thousand sheep, and then agreed jointly to attack the Sun Khan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the envoys back with five hundred horses and a thousand sheep as gifts, and agreed to join in attacking the Sun Khan.

sentences.zh: 阿剌兀思剔吉忽裏先期而至。

translations.literal: Alawusitijihuli arrived ahead of schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Alawusitijihuli arrived ahead of the main army.

sentences.zh: 既平乃蠻，從下中原，復為向導，南出界垣。

translations.literal: After the Naiman were pacified, he followed in reducing the Central Plains, again serving as guide, and went south beyond the border ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: After the Naiman were defeated he joined the conquest of the Central Plains, again serving as guide, and led the army south beyond the border walls.

sentences.zh: 太祖留阿剌兀思剔吉忽裏歸鎮本部，為其部眾昔之異議者所殺，長子不顏昔班並死之。

translations.literal: Taizu left Alawusitijihuli to return and garrison his own tribe; he was killed by tribesmen who had formerly dissented, and his eldest son Buyanxiban died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan left Alawusitijihuli to govern his tribe, but he was killed by former dissenters among his people; his eldest son Buyanxiban died with him.

sentences.zh: 其妻阿裏黑攜幼子孛要合與侄鎮國逃難，夜遁至界垣，告守者，縋城以登，因避地雲中。

translations.literal: His wife Alihei took the young son Xueyaohe and nephew Zhenguo in flight; by night they escaped to the border ramparts, told the guards, were hauled up the wall by rope, and thus took refuge in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Alihei fled with the infant Xueyaohe and nephew Zhenguo. By night they reached the border wall, persuaded the guards to haul them up by rope, and took refuge in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 太祖既定雲中，購求得之，賜與甚厚，乃追封阿剌兀思剔吉忽裏為高唐王，阿裏黑為高唐王妃，以其子孛要合尚幼，先封其侄鎮國為北平王。

translations.literal: After Taizu had secured Yunzhong, he sought them by reward and obtained them, granting gifts very generously; he then posthumously enfeoffed Alawusitijihuli as King of Gaotang and Alihei as Princess of Gaotang; because his son Xueyaohe was still young, he first enfeoffed his nephew Zhenguo as King of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: After Genghis Khan secured Yunzhong he found them through a reward offer and treated them generously. He posthumously enfeoffed Alawusitijihuli as King of Gaotang and Alihei as Consort of the King of Gaotang. Because Xueyaohe was still young, he first enfeoffed the nephew Zhenguo as King of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 鎮國薨，子聶古臺襲爵，尚睿宗女獨木幹公主，略地江淮，薨於軍，賜興州民千餘戶，給其葬。

translations.literal: Zhenguo died; his son Nieguotai inherited the rank, married Ruizong's daughter Princess Dumugan, overran the Jiang-Huai region, died in the army, and was granted more than a thousand households of Xingzhou for his burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenguo died his son Nieguotai inherited the title and married Tolui's daughter Princess Dumugan. He campaigned across the Jiang-Huai region and died on campaign; more than a thousand households of Xingzhou were granted for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 孛要合幼從攻西域，還封北平王，尚阿剌海別吉公主。

translations.literal: Xueyaohe in youth followed in attacking the Western Regions; on return he was enfeoffed King of Beiping and married Princess Alahaibieji.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyaohe campaigned in the Western Regions as a youth and, on his return, was enfeoffed as King of Beiping and married Princess Alahaibieji.

sentences.zh: 公主明睿有智略，車駕征伐四出，嘗使留守，軍國大政，諮禀而後行，師出無內顧之憂，公主之力居多。

translations.literal: The princess was bright and wise in counsel; when the imperial carriage campaigned in all directions she was often left to hold the capital; on great affairs of army and state he consulted and reported before acting; on campaign he had no worry of affairs at home—the princess's power was greatest in this.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was intelligent and resourceful. When the emperor campaigned abroad she often remained as regent; on major military and state affairs he consulted her before acting, and marched without fear for affairs at home—largely through her strength.

sentences.zh: 孛要合未有子，公主為進姬妾，以廣嗣續，生三子：曰君不花，曰愛不花，曰拙里不花。

translations.literal: Xueyaohe had no son; the princess presented concubines to broaden succession, bearing three sons: Junbuhua, Aibuhua, and Zhuolibuhua.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xueyaohe had no sons, the princess presented concubines to secure the succession, and three sons were born: Junbuhua, Aibuhua, and Zhuolibuhua.

sentences.zh: 公主視之，皆如己出。

translations.literal: The princess regarded them all as her own offspring.
translations.idiomatic: The princess treated them all as her own children.

sentences.zh: 孛要合薨，追封高唐王，諡武毅。

translations.literal: Xueyaohe died; posthumously enfeoffed King of Gaotang with posthumous epithet Martial and Resolute.
translations.idiomatic: When Xueyaohe died he was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Gaotang with the epithet Martial and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 後加贈宣忠協力翊衞果毅功臣、太傅、儀同三司、上柱國、駙馬都尉，追封趙王。

translations.literal: Later he was further granted the merit titles Proclaiming Loyalty in Joint Endeavor in Assisting Guardianship, Firm and Resolute, Grand Tutor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Chief Pillar of State, and Consort Commandant, and posthumously enfeoffed King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received the titles Proclaiming Loyalty in Joint Endeavor in Assisting Guardianship, Firm and Resolute, Grand Tutor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Chief Pillar of State, and Consort Commandant, and was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 公主阿剌海別吉追封皇祖姑齊國大長公主，加封趙國。

translations.literal: Princess Alahaibieji was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Princess of Qi and further enfeoffed Princess of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Alahaibieji was posthumously made Imperial Grand-Aunt and Grand Princess of Qi, and further enfeoffed in the Zhao princedom.

sentences.zh: 子君不花，尚定宗長女葉裏迷失公主。

translations.literal: His son Junbuhua married Dingzong's eldest daughter Princess Yelimishi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junbuhua married Güyük's eldest daughter Princess Yelimishi.

sentences.zh: 愛不花，尚世祖季女月烈公主。

translations.literal: Aibuhua married Shizu's youngest daughter Princess Yuelie.
translations.idiomatic: Aibuhua married Kublai's youngest daughter Princess Yuelie.

sentences.zh: 中統初，總兵討阿裏不哥，敗闊不花於按檀火爾歡之地。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong he commanded troops to suppress Arigü; he defeated Kuobuhua at the place Antanhuo'erhuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhongtong era he led troops against Arigü and defeated Kuobuhua at Antanhuo'erhuan.

sentences.zh: 三年，圍李亶於濟南，獨當一面。

translations.literal: In the third year he besieged Li Tan at Jinan, holding one front alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he besieged Li Tan at Jinan and held an entire front by himself.

sentences.zh: 事平，又從征西北，敗叛王之黨撒裏蠻於孔古烈。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he again followed in campaign to the northwest and defeated the rebel prince's partisan Saliman at Kongulie.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed he campaigned again in the northwest and defeated the rebel partisan Saliman at Kongulie.

sentences.zh: 愛不花卒。

translations.literal: Aibuhua died.
translations.idiomatic: Aibuhua died.

sentences.zh: 子闊裏吉思。

translations.literal: His son was Kuolijisi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kuolijisi.

sentences.zh: 闊裏吉思，性勇毅，習武事，尤篤於儒術，築萬卷堂於私第，日與諸儒討論經史，性理、陰陽、術數，靡不該貫。

translations.literal: Kuolijisi by nature was brave and resolute, practiced military affairs, and was especially devoted to Confucian learning; he built a Hall of Ten Thousand Scrolls in his private residence and daily with various scholars discussed the classics and histories, nature and principle, yin and yang, and numerology—there was none he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: Kuolijisi was brave and resolute, skilled in military affairs, and deeply devoted to Confucian learning. He built a Hall of Ten Thousand Scrolls at his residence and daily discussed the classics, history, metaphysics, yin-yang theory, and numerology with scholars—mastering them all.

sentences.zh: 尚忽答的迷失公主，繼尚愛牙失裏公主。

translations.literal: He married Princess Hudeshimi, and afterward married Princess Aiyashili.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Hudeshimi and later Princess Aiyashili.

sentences.zh: 宗王也不幹叛，率精騎千餘，晝夜兼行，旬日追及之。

translations.literal: Imperial Prince Yebugan rebelled; he led more than a thousand elite horsemen, traveling day and night together, and in ten days overtook him.
translations.idiomatic: When Imperial Prince Yebugan rebelled, Kuolijisi led more than a thousand elite horsemen in forced marches day and night and overtook him within ten days.

sentences.zh: 時方暑，將戰，北風大起，左右請待之，闊裏吉思曰：「當暑得風，天贊我也。」

translations.literal: It was then midsummer; about to fight, a north wind rose greatly; those at his side asked to wait; Kuolijisi said: 'In midsummer to obtain wind—Heaven assists me.'
translations.idiomatic: It was midsummer. As battle was about to begin a strong north wind arose. His attendants urged delay, but Kuolijisi said, "A wind in summer heat—Heaven favors me."

sentences.zh: 策馬赴戰，騎士隨之，大殺其眾，也不幹以數騎遁去。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse into battle; horsemen followed; they greatly slaughtered the enemy force; Yebugan fled with a few riders.
translations.idiomatic: He charged into battle at the head of his horsemen, slaughtered the enemy force, and Yebugan fled with only a few riders.

sentences.zh: 闊裏吉思身中三矢，斷其發。

translations.literal: Kuolijisi was struck by three arrows, severing his hair.
translations.idiomatic: Kuolijisi was struck by three arrows that cut through his hair.

sentences.zh: 凱還，詔賜黃金三斤、白金千五百斤。

translations.literal: Returning in triumph, an edict granted three jin of gold and fifteen hundred jin of white metal.
translations.idiomatic: On his triumphant return he was granted three jin of gold and fifteen hundred jin of silver.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，封高唐王。

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne he was enfeoffed as King of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong ascended the throne he was enfeoffed as King of Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 西北不安，請於帝，願往平之，再三請，帝乃許。

translations.literal: The northwest was unsettled; he petitioned the emperor, wishing to go and pacify it; he petitioned again and again, and the emperor then granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: When the northwest grew unsettled he petitioned the emperor to pacify it. After repeated requests the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 及行，且誓曰：「若不平定西北，吾馬首不南。」

translations.literal: As he set out he also swore: 'If I do not pacify the northwest, my horse's head shall not turn south.'
translations.idiomatic: As he departed he swore, "Unless I pacify the northwest, my horse's head shall not turn south."

sentences.zh: 大德元年夏，遇敵於伯牙思之地，眾謂當俟大軍畢至，與戰未晚，闊裏吉思曰：「大丈夫報國，而待人耶！」

translations.literal: In the summer of the first year of Dade he met the enemy at Boyasi; the host said they ought to wait until the great army had fully arrived and fighting would not be late; Kuolijisi said: 'A great man serving the state—yet waiting for others!'
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1297 he met the enemy at Boyasi. His officers urged waiting for the main army, but Kuolijisi said, "A man serving his country does not wait on others!"

sentences.zh: 即整眾鼓躁以進，大敗之，擒其將卒百數以獻。

translations.literal: He immediately arrayed his forces, beat drums, and charged; he greatly defeated them and captured several hundred of their officers and soldiers to present.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately arrayed his troops, beat the drums, and charged, routing the enemy and capturing several hundred officers and men to present as trophies.

sentences.zh: 詔賜世祖所服貂裘、寶鞍，及繒錦七百、介胄、戈戟、弓矢等物。

translations.literal: An edict granted the sable fur coat Shizu had worn, a precious saddle, seven hundred pieces of silk brocade, armor, halberds, bows and arrows, and other items.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted Kublai's own sable coat and precious saddle, seven hundred pieces of brocade silk, armor, halberds, bows, arrows, and other equipment.

sentences.zh: 二年秋，諸王將帥共議防邊，咸曰：「敵往歲不冬出，且可休兵於境。」

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year the princes and generals jointly discussed border defense; all said: 'The enemy in past years did not come out in winter; for now troops may rest at the frontier.'
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the princes and generals discussed border defense. All agreed: "The enemy has not campaigned in winter before; we may rest our troops at the frontier."

sentences.zh: 闊裏吉思曰：「不然，今秋候騎來者甚少，所謂鷙鳥將擊，必匿其形，備不可緩也。」

translations.literal: Kuolijisi said: 'Not so; this autumn the scouting horsemen coming have been very few—what is called when a fierce bird is about to strike, it must hide its form; preparations cannot be delayed.'
translations.idiomatic: Kuolijisi replied, "Not so. This autumn very few scouting parties have appeared. As the saying goes, when a fierce bird is about to strike it conceals itself—we cannot relax our guard."

sentences.zh: 眾不以為然，闊裏吉思獨嚴兵以待之。

translations.literal: The host did not agree; Kuolijisi alone kept his troops strict in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: The others disagreed, but Kuolijisi alone kept his troops on strict alert.

sentences.zh: 是冬，敵兵果大至，三戰三克，闊裏吉思乘勝逐北，深入險地，後騎不繼，馬躓陷敵，遂為所執。

translations.literal: That winter the enemy forces indeed came in great numbers; three battles, three victories; Kuolijisi riding victory pursued north, penetrating deep into dangerous ground; rear horsemen did not follow; his horse stumbled and he fell among the enemy, and thus was captured.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the enemy did arrive in force. Kuolijisi won three battles in succession and pursued the fleeing enemy deep into difficult terrain. His rear guard failed to keep up, his horse stumbled, and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 敵誘使降，惟正言不屈，又欲以女妻之，闊裏吉思毅然曰：「我帝婿也，非帝後面命，而再娶可乎！」

translations.literal: The enemy tempted him to surrender; with upright words he would not yield; they again wished to give him a daughter in marriage; Kuolijisi resolutely said: 'I am the emperor's son-in-law; without the emperor's later command, how could I marry again!'
translations.idiomatic: The enemy urged him to surrender, but he steadfastly refused. When they offered him a daughter in marriage he declared firmly, "I am the emperor's son-in-law—how could I marry again without his express command!"

sentences.zh: 敵不敢逼。

translations.literal: The enemy did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy did not dare press him further.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗遣其家臣阿昔思特使敵境，見於人眾中，闊裏吉思一見輒問兩宮安否，次問嗣子何如，言未畢，左右即引其去。

translations.literal: The emperor once sent his household retainer Axisi as special envoy to the enemy territory; seen among the crowd, Kuolijisi at once upon seeing him asked whether the two palaces were well, next asked how the heir was; before words were finished those at his side immediately led him away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent his household retainer Axisi as special envoy to the enemy territory. Spotted in the crowd, Kuolijisi immediately asked whether the two palaces were well and then how his heir was. Before he could finish speaking, attendants pulled Axisi away.

sentences.zh: 明日，遣使者還，不復再見，竟不屈死焉。

translations.literal: The next day he sent the envoy back and would not see him again; in the end he died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the envoy was sent back and not permitted to see him again. Kuolijisi died unbroken in spirit.

sentences.zh: 九年，追封高唐忠獻王，加贈推忠宣力崇文守正亮節保德功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、駙馬都尉，追封趙王。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as the Loyal and Offering King of Gaotang, further granted the merit titles Loyal in Supporting the Mandate, Illustrious in Culture, Upright in Integrity, Preserving Virtue, Grand Preceptor, Holder of the Office of Equal Ranks with the Three Excellencies, Chief Pillar of State, Consort Commandant, and posthumously enfeoffed as King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was posthumously enfeoffed as the Loyal and Offering King of Gaotang and granted the titles Loyal in Supporting the Mandate, Illustrious in Culture, Upright in Integrity, and Preserving Virtue, along with Grand Preceptor, Equal in Rank to the Three Excellencies, Chief Pillar of State, and Consort Commandant, and posthumously made King of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 公主忽答的迷失追封齊國長公主，愛牙失裏封齊國公主，並加封趙國。

translations.literal: Princess Hudeshimi was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Princess of Qi; Aiyashili was enfeoffed Princess of Qi; both were further enfeoffed as Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Hudeshimi was posthumously made Grand Princess of Qi; Aiyashili was made Princess of Qi; both were further elevated to Princess of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子術安幼，詔以弟術忽難襲高唐王。

translations.literal: His son Shuan was young; an edict had his younger brother Shuhunan inherit the kingship of Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: Because his son Shuan was still young, an edict appointed his younger brother Shuhunan as King of Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 術忽難才識英偉，謹守成業，撫民禦眾，境內乂安。

translations.literal: Shuhunan's talent and insight were heroic and great; he carefully guarded the established enterprise, comforted the people and controlled the masses, and within the borders all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Shuhunan was talented and capable. He carefully preserved the family inheritance, governed the people well, and kept the realm at peace.

sentences.zh: 痛其兄死節，遣使如京師，表請恤典，又請翰林承旨閻復銘諸石。

translations.literal: Grieving his elder brother's death in loyalty to principle, he sent envoys to the capital, memorializing to request favoring rites, and also requested Hanlin Academician Yan Fu to inscribe it on stone.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving his brother's martyrdom, he sent envoys to the capital requesting posthumous honors and asked Hanlin Academician Yan Fu to compose an inscription on stone.

sentences.zh: 教養術安過於己子，命家臣之謹厚者掌其兄之珍服秘玩，待術安成立，悉以付之。

translations.literal: He reared and taught Shuan more than his own sons; he ordered household retainers who were careful and honest to keep his elder brother's precious garments and secret curios, and when Shuan came of age, to deliver them all to him.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Shuan with even greater care than his own sons, entrusted his brother's precious garments and heirlooms to reliable household retainers, and when Shuan came of age delivered them all to him.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，術忽難加封趙王，即以讓術安。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida Shuhunan was further enfeoffed as King of Zhao and immediately yielded it to Shuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 Shuhunan was further enfeoffed as King of Zhao and immediately yielded the title to Shuan.

sentences.zh: 三年，術安襲趙王，尚晉王女阿剌的納八剌公主。

translations.literal: In the third year Shuan inherited the kingship of Zhao and married the Jin Prince's daughter Princess Aladina'erala.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shuan inherited the title King of Zhao and married the Jin Prince's daughter Princess Aladina'erala.

sentences.zh: 一日，召王傅脫歡、司馬阿昔思謂曰：「先王旅殯卜羅，荒遠之地，神靈將何依，吾痛心欲無生，若請於上，得歸葬先塋，瞑目無憾矣。」

translations.literal: One day he summoned the Prince's Tutor Tuohuan and Marshal Axisi and said: 'My late father's coffin sojourns at Boluo, a remote and desolate place—where will his spirit rely? My heart is pained and I wish not to live; if I petition above and may return him for burial at the ancestral mound, I can close my eyes without regret.'
translations.idiomatic: One day he summoned his tutor Tuohuan and marshal Axisi and said, "My father's coffin lies at distant Boluo—where can his spirit rest? My grief is unbearable. If I may petition the throne to bring him home for burial in our ancestral grave, I shall die content."

sentences.zh: 二人言之知樞密院事也裏吉尼以聞，帝嗟悼久之，曰：「術安孝子也。」

translations.literal: The two men reported it to the Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yelijini, who informed the throne; the emperor sighed in grief a long while and said: 'Shuan is a filial son.'
translations.idiomatic: The two reported to Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yelijini, who informed the emperor. The emperor sighed long in grief and said, "Shuan is a filial son."

sentences.zh: 即賜阿昔思黃金一瓶，得脫歡之子失忽都魯、王傅術忽難之子阿魯忽都、斷事官也先等一十九人，乘驛以往，復賜從者鈔五百貫。

translations.literal: He immediately granted Axisi one bottle of gold, and obtained Tuohuan's son Shihudulu, the Prince's Tutor Shuhunan's son Aluhudu, the judicial officer Yexian, and eighteen others—nineteen men in all—to go by relay post; he further granted the followers five hundred strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately granted Axisi a bottle of gold and dispatched nineteen men—including Tuohuan's son Shihudulu, Shuhunan's son Aluhudu, and judicial officer Yexian—by imperial relay. He also granted five hundred strings of paper money to the party.

sentences.zh: 淇陽王月赤察兒、丞相脫禾出八都魯差兵五百人，護其行至殯所，奠告啟視，屍體如生，遂得歸葬。

translations.literal: Prince of Qiyang Yuechicha'er and Chancellor Tuohuchubadulu dispatched five hundred soldiers to escort them to the burial place; offering libation and announcement they opened and viewed—the corpse was as if alive; thus they were able to return him for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qiyang Yuechicha'er and Chancellor Tuohuchubadulu dispatched five hundred soldiers to escort them to the burial place. After libation and announcement they opened and viewed the coffin—the corpse was as if alive—and thus they were able to return him for burial.
